text:
Quinton Byfield, the second overall pick in 2020, has been handed a bigger job in Los Angeles. He is on the ice for 78% of the Kings' power-play chances, up from 44% last season, and he plays 19 minutes a night.

The points have lagged: 6 in 13 games, 0.46 a game against 0.62 last season. The reasons look mostly fixable. His own chances are up to 1.18 expected goals per 60 from 0.82, and at five on five the Kings take 56% of expected goals with him on the ice, almost 9 points better than without him. They have also scored 8.3 fewer goals than those chances deserve while he plays, and it has cost him points.

He is fast, 85th percentile in 20-mph bursts by NHL EDGE, and Evolving-Hockey had him driving play last season, 90th percentile among forwards. His two power-play goals against San Jose on Nov. 4 may be the first sign. Thirteen games is a small sample; the ice time is the part we'd trust.
headline: Byfield has the power play but not the points
